questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman with mitral prolapse is admitted to the hospital for evaluation of her cardiac function. Which of the following values is the best index of the preload on her heart?
questions.solutionHtml:
Left ventricular end-diastolic volume

The gold standard for measuring preload is LV end-diastolic volume.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.571-574

questions.stem: A postlaminectomy patient suddenly stands up after being supine for 8 hours. As a result, which of the following hemodynamic variables will increase?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ejection fraction
  • When a person rises suddenly, blood pools in the dependent portions of the body, causing decreases in venous return, left ventricular end-diastolic volume, stroke volume, and pulse pressure.
  • The reduced stroke volume leads to a drop in cardiac output and, therefore, a drop in blood pressure. Decreased blood pressure produces the baroreceptor reflex, leading to an increase in sympathetic activity which increases heart rate and force of contraction,
  • There is also increased total peripheral resistance.
  • These changes in the cardiovascular system return blood pressure to


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.630–631.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old sedentary, obese male with the four-vessel coronary occlusive disease has a massive myocardial infarction while shoveling snow. In the blizzard conditions, it takes the ambulance over an hour to reach the man’s home. When the paramedics arrive, the patient’s radial pulse is rapid and thready, he has pink froth coming from his mouth, and he is nonresponsive. Increasing which of the following would lead to an increased stroke volume in cardiogenic shock?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ventricular contractility

Stroke volume is influenced by ventricular preload, afterload, and contractility.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.571–576.

questions.stem: A patient comes to his physician complaining that he is no longer able to exercise as long as he used to. The physician auscultates crepitant rales and a third heart sound; blood pressure is normal. He sends the patient to cardiology to rule out heart failure. Which of the following is most consistent with a diagnosis of left heart failure?

options.label: B
options.text: An increased left ventricular wall stress

options.label: C
options.text: An increased left ventricular ejection fraction

options.label: D
options.text: A decreased left ventricular energy consumption

questions.answerText: An increased left ventricular wall stress
questions.solutionHtml:
An increased left ventricular wall stress

Increased left ventricular wall stress leads to left heart failure.

An increased left ventricular wall stress indicates that the left ventricle is working harder than normal to pump blood, which can occur in left heart failure.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.575–576, 586.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true concerning peripheral chemoreceptors?

options.label: A
options.text: Activation is important in inhibiting the diving response

options.label: B
options.text: Activity is increased by increased pH

options.label: C
options.text: They are located in the medulla oblongata, but not the hypothalamus

options.label: D
options.text: Activation is important in the cardiovascular response to hemorrhagic hypotension

questions.answerText: Activation is important in the cardiovascular response to hemorrhagic hypotension
questions.solutionHtml:
Activation is important in the cardiovascular response to hemorrhagic hypotension
  • Carotid bodies are the principal peripheral chemoreceptors for detecting changes in arterial blood oxygen levels, and the resulting chemoreflex is a potent regulator of blood pressure.
  • Reflexes arising from the aortic bodies, which are located in the aortic arch, also regulate cardio-respiratory functions during
  • Thus, carotid and aortic bodies are regarded as the major peripheral chemoreceptors for detecting arterial blood O2 levels and the ensuing reflexes maintain cardio-respiratory homeostasis during hypoxia and hypotension.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 1346.1347,1348

questions.stem: Systolic blood pressure is affected by:-
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above

Systolic blood pressure is affected by Baroreceptors, Chemoreceptors, and Venous Return.

  • The baroreceptors respond rapidly to changes in arterial pressure; in fact, the rate of impulse firing increases in a fraction of a second during each systole and decreases again during diastole.
  • Furthermore, the baroreceptors respond much more to a rapidly changing pressure than to a stationary pressure.
  • That is if the mean arterial pressure is 150 mm Hg but at that moment is rising rapidly, the rate of impulse transmission may be as much as twice that when the pressure is stationary at 150 mm Hg.



Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page Number: 219,222,251.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the vasomotor center (VMC) is true?

options.label: B
options.text: Influenced by baroreceptor signals but not by chemoreceptors

options.label: C
options.text: Acts along with the cardiac vagal center (CVC) to maintain blood pressure

questions.answerText: Acts along with the cardiac vagal center (CVC) to maintain blood pressure
questions.solutionHtml:
Acts along with the cardiac vagal center (CVC) to maintain blood pressure

The lateral portions of the vasomotor center transmit excitatory impulses through the sympathetic nerve fibers to the heart when there is a need to increase heart rate and contractility.




Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page Number: 217.

questions.stem: The carotid sinus baroreceptors are most sensitive to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mean BP

Baroreceptors are sensitive to the rate of pressure change besides the steady or mean pressure. Therefore, at a given mean arterial pressure, decreasing the pulse pressure (systolic minus diastolic pressure) decreases the baroreceptor firing rate.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 1341,1342, 2.

questions.stem: The afferent nerve fibers from the baroreceptors for blood pressure control synapse first at?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nucleus of tractus solitarius

The nucleus tractus solitarii (NTS) receives afferent projections from the arterial baroreceptors, carotid chemoreceptors and cardiopulmonary receptors, and as a function of this information produces autonomic adjustments to maintain arterial blood pressure within a narrow range of variation




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 1341,1342, 2.

questions.stem: What will happen when the common carotid arteries are occluded on both sides?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase in blood pressure and decrease in the heart rate

options.label: B
options.text: Decrease in blood pressure and increase in the heart rate

options.label: C
options.text: Increase in blood pressure and increase in heart rate

options.label: D
options.text: No effect on blood pressure and heart rate

questions.answerText: Increase in blood pressure and increase in heart rate
questions.solutionHtml:
Increase in blood pressure and increase in heart rate
  • A typical reflex change in arterial pressure is caused by occluding the two common carotid arteries.
  • This reduces the carotid sinus pressure; as a result, signals from the baroreceptors decrease and cause a less inhibitory effect on the vasomotor center.



Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page Number: 220

questions.stem: Which of the following are the stimulus for the activation of peripheral chemoreceptors?

options.label: B
options.text: Increased partial pressure of carbon dioxide

options.label: C
options.text: Increase in the concentration of hydrogen ions

questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above

The activation of peripheral chemoreceptors leads to the increased partial pressure of carbon dioxide, an increase in the concentration of hydrogen ions, and Decreased partial pressure of oxygen.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 1347,

questions.stem: The atrial stretch and the cardiopulmonary receptors CAUSE?
questions.solutionHtml:
Both b and c

The atrial stretch and the cardiopulmonary receptors cause vasodilation and Tachycardia.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology 26th Edition Page No 1345,

questions.stem: All of the following statements regarding nitric oxide are true except?

options.label: A
options.text: Causes the Relaxation of the vascular smooth muscle

options.label: D
options.text: NOS 3 is found in endothelial cells

questions.solutionHtml:
Acts by increasing cAMP levels

Nitric oxide doesn’t act by increasing cAMP levels.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 1351,1352,1353.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true regarding the functions of endothelin?

options.label: C
options.text: Endothelin 1 is found in only the brain and the kidneys

options.label: D
options.text: Endothelin 2 is produced primarily by the kidneys and intestine

questions.answerText: Endothelin 1 is found in only the brain and the kidneys
questions.solutionHtml:
Endothelin 1 is found in only the brain and the kidneys

It is found in the brain and kidneys as well as the endothelial cells.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 1354, 1355.
